name: Gling
subcategory: silence and filler-word removal for creator video
tagline: Uploads your raw podcast or talking-head footage, cuts silences, filler words and bad takes, and hands back an edit or a timeline you can open in your NLE.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The expensive-sounding part is the cheap part: silence detection is an ffmpeg filter, and filler words fall out of a local Whisper transcript with word timestamps. An agent can give you a CLI that ingests a file, builds a cut list, renders a rough cut and spits out an EDL or FCPXML in a weekend. What does not fall out for free is the review step: a waveform plus transcript UI where you scrub, unkill a cut, and trust what you are about to export. Bad-take detection, the thing that actually saves hours on a two-hour recording, is a judgment call dressed up as a feature, and your heuristic version will be noticeably dumber. Build it if you record weekly and tolerate a terminal; pay if you need someone else on your team to use it.
coreLoopDIY: Transcribe locally with word-level timestamps, compute a cut list from silence and filler-word rules, then render a rough cut and export an EDL/FCPXML for your editor.
requirements: Python 3.11 and faster-whisper (GPU strongly preferred for long files)
The original media files on local disk
An NLE that imports FCPXML or CMX3600 EDL if you want to refine the cut
whatYouLose: A real review UI: waveform, transcript scrubbing, click to restore a cut
Bad-take detection and best-take selection, which is most of the actual time saved
Clean XML round-trip that survives Premiere, Resolve and Final Cut version quirks
Multi-track and multicam handling, including per-speaker mic cleanup
Someone else's GPUs doing a two-hour transcription while you make coffee
Non-technical collaborators being able to use the thing at all
moatNotes: The moat is not the model, it is the export fidelity and the confidence that the cut list is right before you commit to it.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because editors do not want a cut list, they want a timeline that opens correctly. Getting FCPXML to behave identically across three NLEs and a decade of versions is unglamorous work that nobody wants to redo, and a half-correct XML export costs you more time than manual editing ever did. Add the review UI and the bad-take pass, and the subscription is competing against your Saturday, which it usually wins.
notes: The cutting is a weekend; the trusting is not. Pay for the review UI and the export fidelity, not the silence detector.
prompt:
Build a local CLI tool called "roughcut" that removes silences and filler words from long-form talking-head or podcast video.

Stack, no substitutions: Python 3.11, managed with uv. faster-whisper for transcription. ffmpeg via subprocess for all media work. typer for the CLI. No web server, no accounts, no cloud APIs, no telemetry.

Commands:
1. roughcut transcribe INPUT: transcribe with faster-whisper (model size via --model, default "medium", word_timestamps=True) and write transcript.json next to the input, caching so reruns are free.
2. roughcut plan INPUT: from the transcript plus ffmpeg silencedetect output, build cuts.json: a list of keep-segments with start, end, and a reason for every removed span.
3. roughcut render INPUT: render roughcut.mp4 from cuts.json using ffmpeg concat of stream-copied segments where keyframes allow, re-encoding only at boundaries.
4. roughcut export INPUT --format fcpxml|edl: emit a timeline referencing the ORIGINAL file with the keep-segments as clips, so the cut is editable in an NLE.

Plan rules, all configurable in a roughcut.toml written on first run:
- Drop silences longer than min_silence (default 0.6s), leaving pad_ms (default 120ms) of room tone on each side.
- Drop filler words from a configurable list (um, uh, you know, like, I mean) only when surrounded by silence or sentence boundaries, never mid-phrase.
- Never create a keep-segment shorter than 0.25s; merge instead.
- Snap all cut points to zero crossings in the audio to avoid clicks.

Also print a summary: original duration, output duration, time saved, count of cuts by reason.

Out of scope, do not build: bad-take detection, GUI, waveform viewer, multicam, speaker diarization, subtitle burn-in, uploads.

Include a README with install steps, a sample roughcut.toml, and one worked example on a 60 minute file. Put nothing in .env since nothing needs a secret; if you add one later, document it there.
